statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F = z\vec k through the parameterized surface S, which is oriented toward the z-axis and given, for 0\leq s \leq 1, \ \ 0\leq t\leq 2, by x = 4 s + 5 t, \quad y = 4 s - 5 t, \quad z = s^2+t^2.

static.solution: S is given by \vec r (s,t) = (4 s+ 5 t)\vec i + (4 s- 5 t)\vec j + (s^2+t^2)\vec k, we have \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s} = 4\vec i + 4 \vec j +2 s\vec k \quad\hbox{ and }\quad \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t} = 5 \vec i - 5 \vec j + 2t\vec k, and \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s} \times \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t} = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ 4 \amp 4 \amp 2s\\ 5 \amp -5 \amp 2t \end{array}\right| = (10 s+ 8 t)\vec i +(10 s - 8 t)\vec j - 40 \vec k. Since the \vec i component of this vector is positive for 0 \lt s \lt 1, 0 \lt t \lt 2, it points away from the z-axis, and so has the opposite orientation to the one specified. Thus, we use d\vec A = - \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s} \times \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t} \, ds \, dt, and so we have \int_S \vec F\cdot d\vec A = -\int_0^{2}\int_0^{1} (s^2+t^2)\vec k \cdot \left( (10 s+ 8 t)\vec i +(10 s - 8 t)\vec j - 40 \vec k\right) \,ds\,dt = 40\int_0^{2}\int_0^{1}(s^2+t^2)\,ds\,dt = 40\int_0^{2} \left(\frac{s^3}3+st^2\right) \bigg|_{s=0}^{s=1}\,dt = 40\int_0^{2}(\frac{1}{3} + 1 t^2)\,dt = 40(\frac{1}{3} t+ \frac{1}{3} t^3\bigg|_0^{2} = 40(\frac{2}{3} + \frac{8}{3}) = \frac{400}{3}.
